# Sheetwrite

> Sheetwrite is a framework-agnostic, high-performance spreadsheet grid: a canvas grid backed by a Rust/WASM columnar engine, with an imperative core and React, Vue, and Svelte adapters.

Sheetwrite packages are released together at version 0.6.1. This index is generated from the repository documentation and the compiler-verified public API manifest.

## Full text

- [llms-full.txt](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/llms-full.txt): every authored guide plus every public API declaration in one plain-text file. Fetch this when you need to answer a question or write code.

## Agent workflow

1. Choose one base package for your framework: `@sheetwrite/core` for vanilla, or `@sheetwrite/react`, `@sheetwrite/vue`, or `@sheetwrite/svelte`. Adapters bring core and the WebAssembly engine transitively and expose a package-local `styles.css`. Add optional feature packages, such as `@sheetwrite/xlsx`, only when the relevant guide requires them.
2. Initialize the runtime before mounting a grid. The imperative core awaits `initSheetwrite()` once per document; framework components initialize WebAssembly automatically after client mount, so server-rendered hosts need a client-only boundary.
3. Choose the formula engine once, before the first Grid or store: `@sheetwrite/wasm` is the default; `@sheetwrite/formulas` is the full engine with the analysis families, selected with `import * as formulas from "@sheetwrite/formulas"; await initSheetwrite(undefined, formulas);`. A function the active engine lacks evaluates to `#NAME?`. Read Choose an engine and the Formula function contract before you use a function.
4. Formulas follow the documented Excel rules, not assumptions: `OFFSET`, `INDIRECT`, `RAND`, `RANDBETWEEN`, `TODAY` and `NOW` are volatile and recalculate after each edit; space is the intersection operator, a parenthesized comma list is a union, and `Jan:Mar!B2` is a 3-D reference; a circular reference shows `#CYCLE!` unless the workbook turns on iterative calculation, a document setting that snapshots and XLSX files keep.
5. Built-in chrome is opt-in: `config` shows the toolbar and `config: { ribbon: true }` shows the Excel-style ribbon. XLSX import and export need `@sheetwrite/xlsx` and `import "@sheetwrite/xlsx/register"`; workbook import keeps parts Sheetwrite does not model and writes them back on save.
6. The host owns the document. Sheetwrite never mutates host rows, so read Runtime ownership and Adapter lifecycle before choosing `defaultRows` seeding or explicit `workbook` plus `data`/`datasource` ownership.
7. Readiness is generation-scoped: adapters publish `{ grid, generation, reason }` with reason `initial`, `input-reset`, or `renderer-reset`, and replacing reset-bound inputs replaces the grid. Destroy the grid when its host element's lifetime ends.
8. Verify every symbol, option, event, and error code against the public API declarations in `llms-full.txt` or the generated API pages before using it. Anything absent from those declarations is not public API.
9. Recover through typed errors with stable codes (Error handling), and read Compatibility and limits before claiming Excel, Google Sheets, LibreOffice, or OpenFormula parity.

## Getting started

- [Installation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/installation/): Install Sheetwrite for Vanilla, React, Vue, or Svelte and initialize its WebAssembly runtime.
- [Your first grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/first-grid/): Initialize Sheetwrite, create a workbook, and observe committed changes.
- [Choose an engine](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/choose-an-engine/): Use the default engine for standard formulas or select the full engine for analysis functions.
- [Upgrade to 0.6.0](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/start/upgrade-to-0-6-0/): Review formula recalculation, document protocol, XLSX fidelity, and optional UI changes before upgrading.

## Frameworks

- [Vanilla JavaScript](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/vanilla/): Own Sheetwrite initialization and Grid lifetime without a framework adapter.
- [React](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/react/): Integrate Sheetwrite with React ownership, readiness, and controlled resets.
- [Vue](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/vue/): Use Sheetwrite in Vue: mount the grid component, listen to its events, read the exposed Grid state, and reset it when inputs change.
- [Svelte](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/svelte/): Integrate Sheetwrite with Svelte bindings, callbacks, and reset ownership.
- [Adapter lifecycle](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/frameworks/lifecycle/): Initialization, readiness, resets, and transaction ownership across every Sheetwrite framework adapter.

## Concepts

- [Runtime ownership](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/runtime-ownership/): Understand Sheetwrite runtime, renderer, store, virtualization, and document ownership boundaries.
- [Calculation engine](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/calculation-engine/): Understand engine builds, incremental recalculation, spills, paged data, formula errors, volatility, and iteration.
- [Documents and operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/documents-and-operations/): Understand authoritative workbook snapshots, document operations, storage transactions, and cell inputs.
- [Error handling](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/concepts/error-handling/): Typed failures, stable codes, recovery paths, event direction, validation, and incomplete-data behavior.

## Features

### Grid

- [Grid](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/): Set up the grid, add commands, and control how users select and edit cells.
- [Grid options and presentation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/options-and-presentation/): Configure a grid with GridOptions and choose spreadsheet or data-grid headers.
- [Toolbar and ribbon](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/toolbar-and-ribbon/): Show the built-in toolbar or the Excel-style ribbon in a full or compact layout, all rendered from one command model, and drive host chrome from command state.
- [Selection and keyboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/selection-and-keyboard/): Read and set the selection, navigate with the keyboard, and rebind or add shortcuts.
- [Editing and clipboard](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/editing-and-clipboard/): Edit cells inline, copy and paste with other spreadsheet apps, and undo or redo changes.
- [Custom editors](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/custom-editors/): Replace the stock cell editor with a host-supplied editor for a column.
- [Resize, merge and fill](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/resize-merge-and-fill/): Resize rows and columns, merge cells, and fill a range with the fill handle.
- [Context menu](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/context-menu/): Configure the built-in right-click menu, build your own menu, and draw temporary highlights.
- [Search](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/search/): Find matching cells, step through matches, and replace text from code or with Ctrl+F.
- [Status bar](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/status-bar/): Show Excel-style Average, Count and Sum for the selected cells, or read the totals yourself.
- [Touch](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/touch/): How the Sheetwrite grid turns taps and drags from touch, pen and mouse into scrolling, selection, resizing and fill, and its gesture limits.
- [Grid methods](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/grid/grid-methods/): The imperative Grid handle that createGrid returns, grouped by task: document and sheets, selection and editing, views, layout and lifecycle.

### Formatting

- [Formatting](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/): Set cell styles, fonts, alignment, number formats, and conditional formats.
- [Styles and themes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/styles/): Style the canvas with a theme, CSS custom properties, cell styles, and borders.
- [Fonts and alignment](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/fonts-and-alignment/): Set the font family, size, emphasis, horizontal and vertical alignment, and text wrap of cells.
- [Number formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/number-formats/): Show numbers and dates with Excel-style format codes and an explicit locale.
- [Conditional formats](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formatting/conditional-formats/): Style cells from their values with ordered comparison, text, blank and formula rules.

### Data

- [Data](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/): Sort and filter rows, load data from your own source, validate and protect input, add notes, and save documents with Sheetwrite.
- [Data operations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/data-operations/): Sort, filter, hide, group and aggregate rows, then set frozen panes and zoom.
- [Datasources](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/datasources/): Load rows on demand from an async, cancellable datasource instead of eager data.
- [Keep app rows in your store](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/host-owned-rows/): Keep application row objects in your store while Sheetwrite projects edits through stable row IDs.
- [Validation, protection and notes](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/validation-protection-and-notes/): Restrict what users can enter, protect ranges from local edits, and attach plain-text notes to cells.
- [Persistence and recovery](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/data/persistence/): Persist versioned snapshots and durable pending mutations without confusing session state with document state.

### Formulas

- [Formulas](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/): Write formulas, work with references and arrays, and control recalculation.
- [Authoring and references](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/authoring-and-references/): Store formula sources, use references and local names, and handle scalar values and errors.
- [Operators](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/operators/): Combine values and references with spreadsheet operators, intersections, unions, and 3-D sheet spans.
- [Dynamic arrays and spills](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/dynamic-arrays-and-spills/): Return rectangular formula results and reference their derived spill cells.
- [OFFSET and INDIRECT](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/offset-and-indirect/): Choose reference targets at calculation time with OFFSET and INDIRECT.
- [Volatile functions](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/volatile-functions/): Recalculate random values and runtime references on edits, or supply a fixed UTC clock instant.
- [Iterative calculation](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/iterative-calculation/): Calculate circular references as Excel does: turn on iterative calculation, set the iteration limit and maximum change, and save it in XLSX files.
- [Lookup, criteria, and financial formulas](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/lookup-criteria-and-financial/): Find values, aggregate matching cells, and calculate cash flows with explicit shape and error rules.
- [Analysis formulas](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/formulas/analysis-formulas/): Summarize, forecast, and clean data with the full formula engine. Worked examples for every function family in @sheetwrite/formulas.

### Analysis

- [Analysis](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/): Summarize data in pivot tables and show it in live charts that redraw when cells change.
- [Pivot tables](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/pivot-tables/): Summarize a range or table into a pivot table with rows, columns, values and filters, edit it from the field list, and keep it through undo and sync.
- [Charts](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/analysis/charts/): Add column, bar, line, area, pie, doughnut and scatter charts that read cell ranges and redraw when those cells change; place, move and edit them in the grid.
- [Collaboration and offline work](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/collaboration/): Sequence, persist, acknowledge, retry, and conservatively rebase Sheetwrite document operations.
- [Worker rendering](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/worker-rendering/): Configure OffscreenCanvas worker painting and understand capability-based main-thread fallback.
- [Accessibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/features/accessibility/): Understand the ARIA grid mirror, keyboard behavior, focus, and visible-window accessibility limits.

## Import and export

- [XLSX import](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-import/): Import workbook snapshots or rectangular tables with explicit fidelity warnings.
- [XLSX export](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/xlsx-export/): Download an active-sheet table or save a workbook with formulas and supported formatting.
- [CSV and TSV](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/csv-and-tsv/): Exchange plain table values without installing the optional XLSX package.
- [Kept parts and round trips](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/kept-parts-and-round-trips/): Keep eligible unmodelled XLSX parts as original compressed bytes and surface losses after edits.
- [Large files and streaming](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/large-files-and-streaming/): Read seekable files and write bounded chunks while retaining explicit XLSX resource limits.
- [LibreOffice compatibility](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/import-export/libreoffice-compatibility/): Understand the checked LibreOffice round trips, display fixes and known producer differences.

- [Excel in Node.js](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/tutorials/excel-in-nodejs/): Read real XLSX file bytes and save a workbook snapshot on the server without a DOM.

## Release notes

- [Releases](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/): Release notes for each Sheetwrite version, with new features, changes, fixes, performance results, and upgrade steps.
- [Sheetwrite 0.6.1](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.6.1/): Faster data-grid edits, paged scrolling, text lookups and XLSX rejects, and the upgrade checklist for Sheetwrite 0.6.1.
- [Sheetwrite 0.6.0](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.6.0/): Sheetwrite 0.6.0: charts, pivot tables, reference operators, OFFSET and INDIRECT, iterative calculation, the ribbon, kept XLSX parts and the upgrade checklist.
- [Sheetwrite 0.5.4](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.4/): No more missing source map references, release notes with size charts, and the upgrade checklist for Sheetwrite 0.5.4.
- [Sheetwrite 0.5.3](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.3/): Readable published JavaScript again, package READMEs with install commands for every package manager, and the upgrade checklist for Sheetwrite 0.5.3.
- [Sheetwrite 0.5.2](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.2/): Sheetwrite 0.5.2: smaller npm packages, lower CSV import memory, shifted shortcuts, the Brotli security update and the upgrade checklist.
- [Sheetwrite 0.5.1](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.1/): Sheetwrite 0.5.1: typed shortcuts, busy states and visible command errors, restored column sum speed, new docs and the upgrade checklist.
- [Sheetwrite 0.5.0](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/releases/0.5.0/): Sheetwrite 0.5.0: the full formula engine, spill references, large undo, in-place conflict recovery, engine memory release and the upgrade checklist.

## Public API

- [API reference](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/): Generated reference for every classified Sheetwrite package entry point.
- [`@sheetwrite/charts`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/charts/): 18 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [`@sheetwrite/core`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/core/): 378 exports across 10 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [`@sheetwrite/formulas`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/formulas/): 17 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: internal).
- [`@sheetwrite/react`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/react/): 19 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [`@sheetwrite/svelte`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/svelte/): 19 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [`@sheetwrite/vue`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/vue/): 22 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [`@sheetwrite/wasm`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/wasm/): 15 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: internal).
- [`@sheetwrite/xlsx`](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/api/xlsx/): 7 exports across 2 entry points (primary entry point: supported).
- [Public API declarations](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/llms-full.txt): every export signature grouped by package and entry point. Do not invent symbols absent from it.

- [Data engine performance](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/performance/data-engine/): Ingest, window read, edit, sort, filter, and aggregate timings of the data store.

- [Formula engine performance](https://www.sheetwrite.dev/docs/performance/formula-engine/): Recalculation timings by dependency shape, and how the two engine builds compare.
